author: CraftingTheory
body:
Age: 18

Timezone: GMT / London

Do you have Teamspeak? Yes

Do you have Discord? Yes - on profile (Levrak#4053)

Do you have access to a recording software? Yes - Nvidia Experience (can start recording instantly)



CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION


Do you have any experience as a moderator on other servers?

Only on personal servers I ran myself.


What is your biggest weakness and how will it affect your moderating?

I don't have much knowledge of well known violators and their alts, so first-time punishments may be issued instead of a repeat-offender response. 


What qualities do you think a leader must have? Would you consider yourself a leader? Why/why not?

A leader must be clear and concise in their communication, a good team player, as well as aware of the overall situation. They must be able to look past the immediate effect of their actions and see the long term outcome, and how it contributes to both long term and shrot term goals.


I would consider myself a leader as I have teamwork experience from both inside Avicus and out in the real world. I am good at analysing a situation and seeing possible outcomes from possible actions, and am quick & efficient when communicating, both typing and speaking, to ensure my point gets across clearly.


What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?

I am easy going but mature when necessary, and able to quickly distinguish when a issue requires proper scrutiny and attention.


What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?

I believe a positive & friendly attitude to all newly-met people is important to project a excellent view of the Avicus Network, and a stern but fair & respectful tone towards offenders. Good access to all attributes of the community should be maintained; I am always online on discord and frequently go on teamspeak.

What in your opinion are the three main character traits a moderator must have when moderating?

Alertness, respect, and friendliness.



CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS


You notice a moderator giving out a lot of false bans. They almost always have insufficient evidence or sometimes no evidence and they don’t seem to care. You notice it but other staff members don’t. What would you do?


Bring up the issue with Senior Mods and Admins, record evidence where the other moderator does not to help protect the community from unjust bans, and to be able to show that the moderator is dealing inappropriate punishments. Additional evidence would also help the moderator where they are in the right, and ensuring that actual offenders are not let go without the proper punishment due to lack of evidence. Contact the moderator and advise where they could do more to ensure sufficient evidence is taken.


You are in Teamspeak with a few other players and they begin talking quite disrespectfully about a particular staff member. You agree with what they’re saying to an extent, but the conversation starts to become racial and very disrespectful soon after. You are all in a nightclub channel where this is allowed. What would you do?


Stop contributing to the conversation at hand, and if possible move it on to another topic. Remind the others that race shouldn't be used as a topic of disrespect to others.


You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confidential but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?


Alert a senior staff member, as small harmless leaks pave the way for more important and confidential leaks to be made.


Some senior staff members are in teamspeak joking around with each other. They are removing others ranks, creating certain channels and even harassing certain users. They don’t mean any harm but some players in the channel feel a bit angry that they are using their permissions the way they are. What would you do?


Contact the senior staff members and voice the player's concerns, and recommend that they at least do not disturb or disrupt other player's time in the channel.



CRITERIA 3: OTHER

NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.



Why do you want to be a moderator?

I want to contribute to the Avicus Network beyond donating and also give myself the ability to deal with incidents when other mods aren't on during my timezone.


What does Avicus mean to you?

Avicus is a fun and expansive community, with many closely-knit groups of friends that are welcoming to others. It is where I have met a lot of new and interesting people, and where I hope to meet and help many more.


Anything specific the staff team could do better?

Possibly increase transparency?


Why did you choose to apply at Avicus?

Avicus is my most active minecraft server at the moment, and one where I feel I can have a noticeable impact.


Do you have anything else to add to your application?

N/A
